messages:
alex_sales: Hey team — doing a quick handoff for the MedData POC. They want Private connectivity (no internet egress) from their AWS account to our hosted inference endpoints. Can network/security confirm requirements? -- I have their AWS account ID and subnets below.

maria_neteng: Thanks Alex. Account: 987654321000, VPC cidrs: 10.10.0.0/16 (prod), 10.20.0.0/16 (nonprod). Subnets in prod: 10.10.1.0/24, 10.10.2.0/24. No TGW, single account. They prefer an interface endpoint / PrivateLink if possible. Private DNS is required (api.redwood-inference internal name).

kevin_rd_engineer: @maria_neteng cool. Interface endpoint (AWS VPC Endpoint - com.amazonaws.vpce) is the recommended path. Quick checklist:
- We'll provide the service name (vpce-svc-abc123) for your region.
- Create an Interface VPC Endpoint in your account in the subnets you listed.
- Security groups on the endpoint should allow inbound TCP 443 from your application subnets.
- Enable “Private DNS” on the endpoint so api.redwood-inference resolves to the VPCE ENIs.

kevin_rd_engineer: Sample SG rule: inbound TCP 443 from 10.10.0.0/16. Egress can be 0.0.0.0/0 (or restricted to our ENI CIDRs if your policy requires). No route table changes needed for an interface endpoint (it creates ENIs in the subnets).

maria_neteng: For cross-account: do we need a VPC peering or role? We don't want to open public endpoints.

kevin_rd_engineer: For PrivateLink (interface endpoints) you DON'T need VPC peering. It's cross-account handled by the endpoint service. Customer just creates the VPCE in their account and accepts the service. We will accept connection on our side (service owner). If you prefer VPC peering instead, you'll need route table entries and update security groups — but peering is less desirable for us for hosted infra.

lisa_security: A few security asks from MedData's audit team:
1) Do connections use TLS? (yes)
2) Do you support mTLS? (hosted API: no; we authenticate via API keys over TLS; for Private deployments customer-managed mTLS can be discussed)
3) Can we get an IP allowlist for the VPCE ENIs? (we can provide the VPCE service owner-managed ENI prefixes, but exact secondary IPs are managed by AWS)

kevin_rd_engineer: Confirming answers: TLS terminated by our frontend; API keys used for auth. We can add a VPC-level ACL to restrict egress to the VPCE if they deploy inbound proxies. For the audit, we can produce a short network diagram and the interface endpoint service name/ARN.

alex_sales: MedData also asked about keys for the POC vs Dedicated pool later. For POC we'll provide hosted API keys scoped to the POC org. If they move to Dedicated later we'll discuss cross-account roles + dedicated VPC options.

maria_neteng: One last detail — DNS resolver: should we enable "enableDnsHostnames" and "enableDnsSupport"?

kevin_rd_engineer: Yes, please enable both in the VPC so private DNS overrides work. Also, if you have an outbound proxy or NAT, ensure the proxy allows TLS to our endpoint and does not terminate TLS.

deploy-bot: VPCE service request created: svc-0a1b2c3d in us-east-1. Service owner endpoint ARN: arn:aws:vpce-svc-0a1b2c3d. (automated)

lisa_security: I'll attach the short network/security diagram and the answers to their security questionnaire in this thread by EOD.

alex_sales: Next steps for MedData: 1) Maria to create VPCE in prod subnets and share the endpoint id; 2) Kevin will accept the connection and share SG rules and diagram; 3) Lisa will push the audit doc. I'll loop in CSM for keys distribution. Thanks all :thumbsup:

maria_neteng: Started VPCE creation now, will post VPCE id when ready.

kevin_rd_engineer: FYI if you hit DNS caching issues, do a host flush on app hosts. Also route53 resolver rules not needed for PrivateLink.

alex_sales: Great — keeping this thread as the source of truth for the POC networking handoff. If anything changes ping me.
